subject: Exhibit C workplan and capacity shift request — amendment needed
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthgrid.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Seth Morgan <seth.morgan@healthgrid.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Exhibit C workplan & capacity shift request

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the conversation last week. We're asking Redwood to amend Exhibit C and the associated Order Form to: 1) reallocate 250 dedicated tokens from the EU cluster to the US cluster for Q4; 2) extend the onboarding SOW timeline by three weeks to accommodate our audit window; and 3) add a 90-day burst pool for inference during the product launch.

Attached is a short packet that shows where the capacity should shift and a proposed calendar (HealthGrid_ExhibitC_Request_20261101.pdf). High level requests:
- Effective date: 2026-11-15
- Capacity reallocation: EU -> US, 250 units (exhibit table on p2)
- New temporary burst pool: 90 days, auto-expire unless extended
- SOW change: push the integration milestone by 3 weeks (Section 2.1)

Can you confirm the right internal owners at Redwood for the SOW edits and whether this change will trigger a pricing adjustment or a formal change order? We need a timeline because the launch depends on this.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call.

Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Ops, HealthGrid
elena.rossi@healthgrid.ai
Attachments: HealthGrid_ExhibitC_Request_20261101.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@healthgrid.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit C workplan & capacity shift request

Elena —

Thanks for the clear packet and timeline. We're the right team and I’ve looped in Marcus (customer success / delivery) and Kimberly (legal) for pricing and contract redlines. A few clarifying questions before we draft an amendment:

1) When you say "250 units," is that measured as reserved throughput units (RUs) on the dedicated pool or per-GPU equivalent? It affects the exhibit table conversion.
2) For the 90-day burst pool, do you want automatic billing at usage rates or a prepaid burst credit that we invoice up-front?
3) Any compliance constraints we should mirror in the SOW extension (audit blackout windows or restricted change dates)?

Action plan:
- I’ll coordinate a short internal implementation plan and proposed amendment language by EOD Wednesday.
- Marcus will outline the SOW edits and implementation impact.
- Kimberly will advise on whether this is a change order vs. formal amendment and any language that triggers price adjustments.

I attached a lightly annotated Order Form with placeholders for the Exhibit C changes (redline_orderform_v2.pdf).

If it helps, Marcus and I can propose a mutual action plan with dates for sign-off and cutover. Would Nov 12 for sign-off and Nov 15 for the effective change work on your side?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Attachments: redline_orderform_v2.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

Subject: Proposed SOW edits and capacity implementation plan (draft)

Hi Elena / Naomi,

I pulled together a draft SOW excerpt and a delta document that highlights the Exhibit C table changes and the implementation steps (see exhibit_c-diff.docx). Quick summary of operational impact and proposed dates:

- Sign-off target: 2026-11-12
- Cutover / effective date: 2026-11-15 (as requested)
- Implementation window: 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-18 (3 business days for capacity re-provisioning)
- SOW timeline: integration milestone moved from 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-29 (3-week extension)

Pricing note: because the burst pool request exceeds our standard transient quota, the billing options are: 1) on-demand usage at standard burst rates (+8% unit price uplift for out-of-scope burst), or 2) prepaid burst credits invoiced up-front at a flat rate (we can model both). If HealthGrid prefers 2) we’ll include a prepaid line item in the amendment and a clause to auto-expire the pool after 90 days.

I’ve attached the diff and a short mutual action plan. Kimberly — any concerns on the language around automatic expiry and the update to the Exhibit table? If pricing is accepted, we can prepare an amendment + DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 14:04:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Exhibit C workplan & capacity shift request — proposed redlines

Naomi / Marcus / Elena —

Thanks for the context and the draft materials. I reviewed the exhibit table delta and the proposed SOW dates. High level legal guidance and next steps:

1) This is a contract amendment (not a simple PO change) because it modifies Exhibit C and the SOW milestone dates. We should produce a one‑page Amendment + redlined Order Form that references MSA v2.1, includes the new Exhibit table, and captures the prepaid-burst option if HealthGrid chooses it.

2) Pricing language: if HealthGrid selects the on-demand burst, we need an explicit uplift clause (Marcus’s +8% callback is fine). For the prepaid option, we need: - invoicing term (Net 30), - non-refundable statement for unused credits after expiry, and - an auto-expire clause at 90 days.

3) Operational and audit language: add a short sentence in Section 2.1 of the SOW to preserve HealthGrid's audit blackout window (2026-11-10 to 2026-11-14). That prevents change implementation during that period and aligns the milestone shift.

4) Deliverables: I attached redline_orderform_v3.pdf with recommended language (tracked snippets in the doc). Please review. Once you confirm the pricing option and operational blackout wording, I’ll prepare the Amendment and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Next steps / timeline proposal:
- Nov 8: HealthGrid confirms prepaid vs on-demand burst option and PO intent
- Nov 10: Team finalizes amendment text (legal / commercial)
- Nov 12: Sign-off and DocuSign send
- Nov 15: Effective date

Elena — can you confirm whether HealthGrid will sign on behalf of procurement by Nov 12 and whether you prefer prepaid credits or on-demand? If procurement needs a PO first, let Naomi know and we’ll coordinate billing and the invoice flow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
